target_customer: Consumers with large media libraries and multiple devices
problem: Music and files were stuck on one computer; users wanted to stream and sync media from cloud storage across devices.
business_model: Freemium cloud storage with paid tiers

competitors.name: Dropbox
competitors.what: File sync service on Amazon S3
competitors.traction_then: Leading consumer sync service by early 2009

technical_complexity.rationale: Client sync and media streaming from cloud storage across desktop and mobile platforms was standard but wide engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Many sync and storage rivals, low switching costs, built on commodity cloud storage.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Motorola Mobility bought the team and technology in Dec 2010 to integrate with Motoblur devices; the ZumoDrive service later ended.

market_need_then: Early 2009 coverage compared it with Dropbox and praised its price and features, showing demand for cloud media access.

branding.domain_note: Product name ZumoDrive; trademark later held by Motorola and cancelled 2017
branding.community_and_virality: No sourced evidence of community or merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Little branding evidence; overshadowed by Dropbox.

outcome_analysis: Zecter built ZumoDrive for streaming and syncing media, launched in early 2009 into a field with Dropbox, SugarSync and Box.net, and raised a reported $1.5M Series A in December 2009. Motorola Mobility acquired the company on 2010-12-22, and the ZumoDrive service later ended. The exit looks like a technology and team deal rather than a win in the consumer storage race.
notes: YC page lists no website and the product is defunct. Round details come from Seedtable and search summaries of TechCrunch and FinSMEs; CB Insights total $2.52M and its YC listing unverified. CB Insights lists other cofounders (Vijay Mani); not on the YC page so not recorded. Competition is as of the Feb 2009 launch because no source dated to the 2007 batch was found. Service end date reported as about 2012, not confirmed.
